messages.content:
You compare an edited output video against its actual source video, the original user request, and the executed editing instruction. Optional reference assets show the desired editing target.
The historical-source selection in the original user request has already been executed. Evaluate only its editing requirements against the actual videos. Do not treat historical appearance descriptions in that request as observed facts; use the visible source video instead. Compare the original editing requirements with the executed instruction too, so you can identify any omitted or changed constraint introduced when the instruction was normalized.
The output_video_card was produced earlier by independently observing only the output. Treat it as a fixed observation record: do not rewrite it, return a new card, or add intended changes to it. It can be imperfect; inspect the actual videos when comparing.
Call record_edit_result exactly once. Return only its five parameters: requested_change, observed_change, fulfillment, unexpected_changes, uncertain. These describe the source-to-output comparison, not a new video card. Use concise English.
State what was requested and what visibly changed. Use fulfillment=fulfilled, partial, not_fulfilled, or uncertain. Do not infer success from the instruction. Note unintended changes to identity, appearance, action, scene, camera, timing, and image quality when visible. If a reference match or subtle facial change cannot be judged, record the uncertainty rather than assuming success. Do not claim to have inspected missing reference pixels. Do not call an editing tool or regenerate video.
Use one separate XML parameter block for each of the five parameters. The three text parameters contain text. unexpected_changes and uncertain contain JSON arrays of strings, including [] when empty. Do not nest a card or review object inside any parameter.
Structural example only; replace descriptions with your actual comparison:
<tool_call>
<function=record_edit_result>
<parameter=requested_change>Requested edit</parameter>
<parameter=observed_change>Actual visible change</parameter>
<parameter=fulfillment>uncertain</parameter>
<parameter=unexpected_changes>[]</parameter>
<parameter=uncertain>["Any unresolved comparison"]</parameter>
</function>
</tool_call>

content.text: {"executed_editing_prompt":"Change the person's hairstyle to the one shown in the reference images, using the front view for the front shape and the back view for the back shape. Transfer only the hairstyle shape and structure from the references; do not adopt the reference person's facial features, hair color, or clothing. Preserve the person's existing hair color, identity, and all other elements of the current video.","history_selection_status":"Already executed. Only compare editing requirements; historical appearance words are not observed facts.","original_user_request":"Please use the video where the person has red hair as the starting point and make the following change: Using the provided source video, apply the following edit: I'd like to change the person's hairstyle to the one shown in the reference images. Only transfer the hairstyle from the reference images, not the reference person's facial features, hair color, or clothing. Preserve everything else in the current video.","output_video_card":{"observed":{"action":"The character stands with one arm raised overhead and steps forward along a glowing white floor line.","camera":"Medium full shot from the side, with the camera slowly pulling back to reveal more of the floor.","clothing":"A dark blue two-piece outfit consisting of a cropped tank top and a short skirt.","hair_color":"Red.","hairstyle":"Shoulder-length wavy hair with a side part.","identity":"A 3D animated female character with a slim build, shown in profile facing right.","scene":"A futuristic indoor space with a glossy purple floor, white grid lines, and neon-lit purple and blue walls and structures."},"uncertain":[]}}

arguments.observed_change: The character's hair changed from a short cropped style to a shoulder-length, side-parted wavy style consistent with the reference shape. The hair remains red, and the outfit, pose, scene, camera movement, and overall identity appear unchanged.
arguments.requested_change: Change the person's hairstyle to the reference shape, using the front and back views for structure, while preserving the person's existing red hair color, identity, clothing, and all other video elements.
uncertain: The exact back shape could not be fully verified because the character is shown mostly in profile.
